scope: Selected paper candidate models and recorded optimizer inputs, not a full reproduction archive or an exact-certificate workflow.
method_full_name: Quantum Estimator Design via Stiefel Adam–RCG Optimization with Certified Risk Bounds
measurement_count_definition: The paper's s is the number of rows in Z before deleting tiny effects or merging directions. Historical keys M and Q store s and Z; s is not a minimum-outcome claim or the SOS level m.

notation.n: Hilbert-space dimension; 2^N for N qubits, 3 for a qutrit
notation.d: Number of parameters; 3 for full qubit models, 8 for full qutrit models
notation.s: Outcome count, stored as M or M_by_N; dual_input_M is a separate candidate's s
notation.Z: Stiefel frame, saved as Q; the POVM is M=(M_x), with M_x=Z^dagger e_x e_x^dagger Z
notation.D_tilde_and_F_tilde: Transformed-coordinate derivatives and Fisher matrix, saved as D and F in candidate files
notation.c_num: Floating-point weighted candidate risk, saved as paper_risk after applying risk_scale
notation.m: SOS denominator exponent, called level in the fixed-coefficient SOS API
notation.trace: tr for operators on the Hilbert space; Tr for matrices on parameter space

selection: Smallest finite final risk among the specified random seeds. Nonconverged finite endpoints remain eligible; preserve their status.
unknown_settings_policy: null means the executed historical value was not recorded. Execution requires an explicit CLI override. The current optimizer default is not evidence of that historical value.

kernel_conventions.adam: Projected ambient Adam, moments not transported, last iterate; beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
kernel_conventions.rcg: PR+ with projection transport and descent restart
kernel_conventions.stopping: Gradient tolerance, iteration cap, line-search failure or nonfinite status; no Fisher ridge or probability clipping

experiment1.optimizer_coordinates: Single-copy SLD-normalized local tangents, J_1=I; no additional weight whitening
experiment1.paper_coordinates: Returned reporting coordinates are the SLD-normalized eta coordinates with W=N I; the paper also gives the equivalent expression in standard Bloch theta coordinates
experiment1.paper_risk: c_num=N Tr(F_tilde^-1)=Tr(J_theta0^(N) V_theta0^(N)); F_tilde is F_optimizer and J_theta0^(N)=N diag(1,1,1/(1-r^2)) in Bloch coordinates
experiment1.history_note: The r=1/2 points reused experiment2. The example runner computes a new candidate at one chosen point; it does not reproduce the original concurrent timing or the Vidal/NH comparison.

experiment2.optimizer_coordinates: Single-copy SLD-normalized local tangents, J_1=I; no additional weight whitening
experiment2.paper_coordinates: Returned reporting coordinates are the SLD-normalized eta coordinates with W=N I; the paper also gives the equivalent expression in standard Bloch theta coordinates
experiment2.paper_risk: c_num=N Tr(F_tilde^-1)=Tr(J_theta0^(N) V_theta0^(N)); F_tilde is F_optimizer and J_theta0^(N)=N diag(1,1,1/(1-r^2)) in Bloch coordinates
experiment2.history_note: The optimizer runs on the unscaled objective; multiplying its tangents by 1/sqrt(N) before optimization would change the historical gradient and stopping scale. Apply N only to the reported risk.

experiment3_diagonal.historical_transform: eigh(W); T=(U/sqrt(eigenvalues))@U.T; no extra symmetrization in this historical driver
experiment3_diagonal.paper_risk: c_num=(153/223) Tr(F_tilde^-1); cost per two-copy block, no extra factor 2; F_tilde denotes F_optimizer in the historical transformed coordinates
experiment3_diagonal.history_note: All ten s=24 runs recorded learning rate 0.005 and no retries. The selected s=24 candidate and the s=16 dual-input candidate are distinct. Ideal rational-weight and coordinate transfer require separate certification; binary64 matrices here are numerical inputs.

experiment3_nondiagonal.historical_transform: eigh(W); T=(U/sqrt(eigenvalues))@U.T; symmetrize T and the transformed derivatives
experiment3_nondiagonal.paper_risk: c_num=Tr(W F_Bloch^-1)=Tr(F_tilde^-1); cost per two-copy block, no extra factor 2; F_tilde denotes F_optimizer in the historical transformed coordinates
experiment3_nondiagonal.history_note: The retry candidates and the driver's current default do not identify the executed settings. The auxiliary s=13 warm_reference is outside the adopted ten random starts and is not provided by this runner.

experiment4_A.paper_coordinates: Full eight-parameter orthonormal adapted Gell-Mann basis, tr(D_i D_j)=delta_ij; original derivatives stored as D0
experiment4_A.historical_transform: eigh(W); T=(U/sqrt(eigenvalues))@U.T; symmetrize T and the transformed derivatives
experiment4_A.paper_risk: c_num=Tr(W F_GMM^-1)=Tr(F_tilde^-1); one qutrit, no copy-number factor; F_tilde denotes F_optimizer in the historical transformed coordinates
experiment4_A.history_note: The outcome count s includes tiny effects and is counted before deletion/merging. Only the adopted random starts are implemented; historical auxiliary warm starts and the symmetric dual-input B projection are not part of this candidate runner.

experiment4_B.paper_coordinates: Full eight-parameter orthonormal adapted Gell-Mann basis, tr(D_i D_j)=delta_ij; original derivatives stored as D0
experiment4_B.historical_transform: eigh(W); T=(U/sqrt(eigenvalues))@U.T; symmetrize T and the transformed derivatives
experiment4_B.paper_risk: c_num=Tr(W F_GMM^-1)=Tr(F_tilde^-1); one qutrit, no copy-number factor; F_tilde denotes F_optimizer in the historical transformed coordinates
experiment4_B.history_note: Only A and B are adopted in experiment4. The candidate runner does not implement analytical bounds, attainability constructions, or other historical examples.
